The time auto-completer is fun because it indulges your playful exploration. (01:04:06): In onboardings, it wasn't long before I saw people asking, "What can it do? Where does it break? How does it work? What happens if I keep on typing in a series of tens? Well, it turns out that's October the 10th at 10:10 PM. Well, how about a series of twos? Well, that's February the second, 2022 at 2:00 PM." Then you start trying more complex inputs like in a fortnight and a day, and that works, which is a pleasant surprise. And it's not long before you find more pleasant surprises like time zone math happens without you thinking about it. You can just type in 8:00 AM in Tokyo and it turns out that's 8:00 PM Eastern Time and you no longer have to do the time zone math. (01:04:45): Then most people were really delighted to find out that if you really want, you can snooze emails until never, i.e. you can literally type in never, and the email will never come back. It had like a little shrug emoji at the same time. Is this toy going to win awards? Nope. But is it fun actually, surprisingly yes. So what I would encourage people to do is, think about the features of their product. Do those features indulge, playful, exploration? Are they fun even without a goal? And do they elicit moments of pleasant surprise? If so, you have a toy and you can combine that with other toys and actually start to build a game.
turns.zh: 嗯，也许大家不知道，在成为创始人之前——你们应该能猜到——我曾是一名职业游戏设计师。结果发现，没有统一的游戏设计理论。创造游戏需要借鉴艺术、心理学、数学、叙事设计等领域的知识。在Superhuman，我们确定了五个核心关注点：目标、情感、玩具、控制和流畅性。在这些方面，我们总结了许多游戏设计原则。其中一个例子是，制作有趣的玩具，然后将它们融入游戏中。（01:03:12）：我喜欢问的一个问题是，玩具和游戏是一样的吗？它们看起来确实不同。例如，我们玩玩具，但我们玩的是游戏。球是玩具，但足球是游戏。结果发现，最好的游戏都是由玩具构成的。为什么？因为这样它们在两个层面上都很有趣——玩具层面和游戏本身。所以在Superhuman，我们最喜欢的玩具之一是时间自动补全功能。如果你使用Superhuman，当你按H键、设置邮件提醒或打盹时，会出现这个功能。你可以输入任何内容，哪怕是乱码的，它也会尽力理解。比如输入2D，就变成两天；3H是三小时；one MO是一月。时间自动补全功能很有趣，因为它能满足你玩耍探索的需求。（01:04:06）：在入职流程中，不久我就发现有人问：“它能做什么？哪里会出错？怎么操作？如果我连续输入一连串数字会怎样？”结果发现，那是2022年2月2日下午2点。而如果输入一连串2，就变成了2022年2月2日下午2点。然后你开始尝试更复杂的输入，比如“两周加一天”，这也成功了，真是惊喜。很快你会发现更多惊喜，比如时区计算无需你费心思。你只需输入东京时间上午8点，就能发现对应的是美国东部时间晚上8点，再也不用自己计算时区了。（01:04:45）：然后大多数人都很高兴地发现，如果你愿意，甚至可以把邮件永久打入冷宫——即输入“never”，邮件就再也不会回来了。它甚至会同时显示一个小耸肩表情。这玩具能获奖吗？不。但它确实很有趣，出乎意料地有趣。所以我鼓励大家思考产品的功能。这些功能能满足人们的玩耍探索欲吗？即使没有目标，它们本身有趣吗？能引发令人愉悦的惊喜时刻吗？如果是，那你就找到了玩具，然后可以把它们和其他玩具结合起来，真正开始打造游戏。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: If people were to listen to this segment of the podcast, they would never guess we're talking about B2B software and email, which I love. Let's talk about pricing strategy and your approach to pricing. Another very contrarian approach that you guys took where you charge $30 a month for email that was free, that people don't need to pay for anywhere. And it's worked and now a lot of companies are thinking of it this way. You've even raised your prices recently. What have you learned about pricing strategy that you think might be helpful to folks?
turns.zh: 如果人们听了这段播客，他们绝对猜不到我们在谈论B2B软件和邮件，而这正是我热爱的。让我们聊聊定价策略和你们的定价方法。你们采取了一个非常反常规的做法，把免费的邮件服务定价为每月30美元，用户在其他地方根本无需付费。结果证明这很有效，现在很多公司都在效仿。你们甚至最近提价了。在定价策略方面，你们学到了什么，觉得对大家有帮助吗？

turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: I always say the same thing when it comes to pricing, which is before you figure out pricing, you must first figure out positioning. Superhuman is the best email tool on the market. We fortunately have the metrics to show this. One of the cool things about selling an email tool, is you can compare the 30 days prior to using Superhuman to the 30 days after, or the year before to the year after. We do that obviously. We're able to show that people get through their email twice as fast with Superhuman, that they respond one to two days faster, and that they save four hours or more every single week. Because of that, we're very confident in saying that Superhuman is the best email tool on the market and that we're building it for high performing teams and high performing individuals. In other words, we serve the high end of the market. (01:06:48): Once you understand your positioning, you can then move on to pricing. And one of the best books on this is a book called Monetizing Innovation by Madhavan Ramanujam. And Madhavan covers a lot of ways to develop pricing. We used one of the easiest methods, which is the Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity [inaudible 01:07:08]. In the early years, we asked, I think it was around a hundred of our earliest users, the following four questions. Number one, at what price would you consider Superhuman to be so expensive that you would not consider buying it? Number two, at what price would you consider Superhuman to be priced so low that you'd be worried about its quality and you wouldn't buy it? At number three, what price would you consider Superhuman to be starting to get expensive, so that it's not out of the question, but you'd have to give some thought to buying it? And number four, at what price would you consider Superhuman to be a bargain? A great buy for the money?, (01:07:45): Now most startups orient around price point number four. This is especially true for greenfield opportunities, marketplaces, you've got to set the transaction value around price 0.4. Basically when you want as many people to sign up as is humanly possible, at the top of the funnel. But the price point that supports our best in class, best in category position, is actually the third one. It starts to feel expensive, but then you sit down and you think about the time that you spend in email, the ROI, and you still buy it anyway. It turns out that the median answer for the third question was $30 per month, and that's how we picked our price. (01:08:27): And once we picked our price, we then do a quick gut check on market size. For example, we're a venture scale company, but at the time the question that we had to ask is, "Could we grow into a billion dollar valuation?" Well, let's assume that at that point our valuation is 10 times our ARR, so our ARR would have to be a hundred million dollars. Well, that would be 300,000 subscribers at $30 per month. That is conservatively assuming no other ways to increase ARP. You mentioned price increase, you can also go up market, you can sell new products and so on. We asked ourselves, without those tricks, do we think we can get to hundreds of thousands of subscribers? And we answered emphatically, yes, so we went ahead with that price.
turns.zh:
谈到定价，我总是强调一件事：在确定定价之前，你必须先明确产品定位。Superhuman是市面上最好的邮件工具。我们很幸运能用数据来证明这一点。卖邮件工具的好处之一是，你可以对比使用Superhuman前30天和使用后30天的数据，或者前后年度的数据。我们确实这么做了。我们能证明，使用Superhuman的人处理邮件速度快了一倍，回复速度快了一到两天，每周节省至少4小时时间。因此，我们非常有信心地说，Superhuman是市面上最好的邮件工具，我们的产品专为高效团队和高绩效个人打造。换句话说，我们服务的是高端市场。

（01:06:48）一旦你理解了产品定位，就可以转向定价策略了。在这方面，Madhavan Ramanujam的《创新变现》一书堪称经典。书中提到了多种定价策略。我们采用了最简单的方法——范·韦斯特多普价格敏感度分析法。在初期，我们向大约100名早期用户提出了四个问题：
1. 你认为Superhuman价格高到让你无法考虑购买的临界点是多少？
2. 你认为Superhuman价格低到让你担心质量而不会购买的临界点是多少？
3. 你认为Superhuman价格开始偏高、值得考虑购买的临界点是多少？
4. 你认为Superhuman价格足够低、物有所值的临界点是多少？

（01:07:45）大多数初创公司都围绕第四种定价策略展开布局，尤其是在绿地市场和平台型市场中，往往将交易价值定在0.4倍价格。毕竟，目标是在漏斗顶端尽可能多地获取用户。但支持我们打造顶级产品的定价策略其实是第三种。用户会觉得价格偏高，但经过深思熟虑后，他们会意识到节省的邮件处理时间和ROI远超价格。最终，我们将第三个问题的中位数定为每月30美元，并据此设定了价格。

（01:08:27）确定价格后，我们迅速评估了市场规模。作为风险投资级别的公司，我们需要判断能否成长至10亿美元估值。假设估值是ARR的10倍，那么ARR必须达到1亿美元。以每月30美元计算，这对应30万订阅用户。即便不考虑其他增量措施，我们也有信心达到这个目标。因此，我们坚定地选择了这个价格。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, there's a couple more things I want to chat about in the time that we have and then I know you have to run. One is around AI and the work you guys are doing there. I know that's been a big unlock. And then two, the stuff you're doing in the enterprise. Then if we have time, there's a question I want to ask that I think is a really interesting way you guys operate. (01:09:29): Let's talk about AI first. It feels like there's this being in the right place at the right time. It feels like you guys have been building this for a while, and then AI just unlocked another stage in what you're able to do with email. Just talk about what you've done and what how you think about AI integrating into what you're doing, how it's enabled you to kind of take off again?
turns.zh: 好的，在剩余的讨论时间里，我还想聊几件事，然后我知道你们得赶时间了。第一件事是关于人工智能以及你们团队在这方面的工作。显然，这是一个重大的突破。第二件事是你们在企业领域的业务。如果时间允许，我还想问一个问题，我觉得你们的运营方式非常有趣。（01:09:29）：我们先来谈谈人工智能。这感觉就像是天时地利的完美结合。看起来你们已经为此埋头研发了一段时间，而人工智能的应用让你们在邮件处理方面又迈进了一个新阶段。能否分享一下你们在这方面的成果，以及如何将人工智能融入现有业务中，从而实现新的突破？

turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: It's true that sometimes startups boil down to being in the right place at the right time. We actually had a massive AI launch recently about two weeks ago, but even before then we had multiple flagship AI features. Our first AI feature was write with AI, jot down a few words and we'll turn them into a fully written email. We actually match the voice and tone in the emails you've already sent. So unlike Co-pilot, unlike Gemini, unlike basically every other email app, the email sounds like you. This AI feature is way more popular than I expected it to be. On average today, users are using it 37 times per week. (01:10:33): Number two, our next AI feature was auto summarize, which shows a one line summary above every conversation. And as new emails arrive, it updates instantly. Again, unlike Co-pilot and Gemini, it's pre-computed. One of the things we do is, we go above and beyond to make these features really premium and feel amazing. The next AI feature after that was instant reply. Imagine waking up to an inbox where every email already has a draft reply. You would simply edit and then send, and sometimes you wouldn't even need to edit. I can share because we just finished this analysis, that over 2024, the percentage of emails that are AI written and sent with Superhuman has grown four times just in one year. (01:11:20): Then if I remember correctly, the feature after that was Ask AI. Email of course, is this treasure trove of critical information, things like project statuses, customer communication, meeting updates, deal execution, and so much more. And for over 40 years we've had to rely on what we hilariously call, search. You have to remember senders, guess keywords, scan subject lines, and now you can just ask, "Where is the queue one offsite?" or, "What are my flight details?" Or, "What is the top five most positive customer responses to the Ask AI launch?" A task by the way, which previously used to take me 20 or 30 minutes to read through all the emails and then create that report now happening in less than five seconds. (01:12:09): Recently we, like I said, announced our biggest evolution yet. Superhuman AI is constantly helping you. It's organizing your inbox. It's also making sure you never drop the ball. We have things that we call Auto Labels. You can now write a short prompt like job applications or requests to review work, and you can then immediately see when emails match that prompt, when people apply for a job or they ask you to review work. With Auto Reminders, if your email needs a response, Superhuman will now automatically set a reminder. You don't have to remember to do that and you'll never drop the ball again. All you need to do is hit send. With Auto Drafts, Superhuman will now automatically draft your follow-up emails for you and will soon be drafting replies to basically every email that needs a response. (01:12:59): And finally, with what we call Workflows, you can now turn email into repeatable automated workflows. For example, I often get emails from people who are interested in working at Superhuman, and I would normally reply to that candidate and I would let them know that the team will take a look. I'll then forward to the original message, including any resume or any letter to our head of people and operations and ask her to reach out, if interested. With Workflows, I can now automate this entire process. It's, you can imagine, creating a little flowchart of what has to happen. Not only does that save a huge amount of time, with Workflows you don't even have to be in your inbox. In fact, you don't even have to be working. You could be on vacation while Superhuman AI is working for you.
turns.zh:
确实，有时候初创公司的成功确实取决于"在正确的时间出现在正确的地点"。实际上，我们最近两周前刚推出了大规模的AI功能，但在此之前我们就已经推出了多个旗舰级AI功能。我们的首个AI功能是"AI写信"——只需输入几个关键词，它就能自动生成一封完整的邮件。关键是，系统会模仿用户已发送邮件的语气和风格。这与Co-pilot、Gemini等邮件应用截然不同——我们的AI生成的邮件听起来就是用户自己的声音。这个功能的受欢迎程度远超我们的预期。如今用户平均每周使用37次。（01:10:33）第二个AI功能是"自动摘要"，它能在每段对话上方显示一行摘要。新邮件到达时，摘要会即时更新。与Co-pilot和Gemini不同，这个功能是预先计算好的。我们尤其注重提升这些功能的用户体验，让它们真正成为优质服务的典范。接下来是"即时回复"功能。想象一下，当你醒来时收件箱里每封邮件都已准备好回复草稿。你只需编辑后发送，有时甚至无需修改。我可以透露，2024年全年，我们通过Superhuman生成并发送的AI邮件比例仅用一年就增长了四倍。（01:11:20）然后如果我没记错的话，接下来是"AI问答"功能。邮件无疑是关键信息的宝库，比如项目状态、客户沟通、会议更新、交易执行等重要信息。40多年来，我们不得不依赖所谓的"搜索"功能——记忆发件人、猜测关键词、扫描主题行。而现在你只需问："离线会议的队列在哪儿？"、"我的航班详情是什么？"、"AI问答功能上线后，前五名最积极的用户反馈是什么？"这样一个任务，过去需要花20到30分钟浏览所有邮件并生成报告，现在不到五秒钟就能完成。（01:12:09）最近我们如我所说宣布了迄今最大规模的进化。Superhuman的AI功能不断为你提供帮助：整理收件箱、确保你不会遗漏任何任务。我们推出了"自动标签"功能，你可以输入简短提示，如"求职申请"或"审阅工作请求"，系统会立即匹配符合条件的邮件。当有人申请工作或请求审阅时，你能第一时间收到通知。通过"自动提醒"功能，系统会自动为需要回复的邮件设置提醒，让你无需手动操作。所有你需要做的就是点击发送。还有"自动草稿"功能，系统会自动为你起草后续邮件，很快将为所有需要回复的邮件起草回复。（01:12:59）最后，通过"工作流"功能，你可以将邮件转化为可重复的自动化工作流程。例如，我经常收到对在Superhuman工作感兴趣的人的邮件，通常会回复告知团队会查看申请，并将邮件转发给人力运营负责人让她跟进。现在通过工作流，我可以自动化整个流程。你可以想象，这就像创建一个流程图，明确每个步骤。不仅节省大量时间，而且无需一直查看收件箱。事实上，用户甚至可以完全脱离收件箱进行操作。
甚至不必工作。当超人级人工智能为你工作时，你大可以去度假。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This sounds like product market fit to me. This all sounds wonderful. It just makes sense. This is the stuff we've been promised, our underwater cities and flying cars and then just email that just works magically and replies for us and all these things. I love all these things you're doing. (01:14:08): For folks that are building with AI. I'm curious, what's maybe been the biggest surprise, either good or bad, building so deeply on top of AI models that you think might be helpful for folks to just, "Watch out for this," or, "Hey, check this out."?
turns.zh: 听起来这像是产品与市场完美契合。这一切听起来都很棒，逻辑清晰。这正是我们一直被承诺的东西——水下城市、飞行汽车，再到能神奇回复邮件的邮箱应用。你们正在做的这些东西真是太棒了。（01:14:08）对于那些在人工智能领域开发的人来说，我很好奇，在深度依赖人工智能模型后，最大的惊喜——无论是好的还是坏的——是什么？或许有些东西值得提醒大家注意，比如“小心这个”或者“看看这个”。

turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: I think for me the biggest surprise has been how unpredictable the user love has been in terms of what they love and what they don't love. For example, write with AI. This sounds like a commodity feature and on all surface level it is. Every email app, every writing surface has a write with AI feature in. I would wager ours is the best at emails and surprisingly that's what we do. But the surprising thing was just how much people love it and how often it gets used. 37 times per user per week is still mind-blowing to me. I had not expected that, so that's the most surprising thing. (01:15:11): And on the flip side, there were certain AI features where I did expect a ton of usage, but we didn't quite get the usage that we were perhaps hoping for. Hopefully I'm not AI Kramer, but basically everything I thought would work out well, people use it less than they thought they did. And everything where I was like, "I don't know, but let's build the thing," people love that.
turns.zh: 对我来说，最大的惊喜是用户对产品的喜爱程度超出预期。比如，写作助手功能。这听起来像是一个普通的功能特性，从表面看确实如此。每个邮箱应用、每个写作平台都有类似的写作助手功能。我敢打赌，我们的邮箱应用在这方面做得最出色，但令人惊讶的是，它被如此频繁地使用。每位用户每周使用37次，这个数字至今仍让我感到震惊。我完全没想到会这样，所以这是最令人惊讶的地方。（01:15:11）另一方面，某些人工智能功能的使用量远低于我们的预期。希望我不是那个“人工智能克莱默”，但基本上所有我认为会大受欢迎的功能，人们实际使用的频率都比预期的低。而那些我说“我不知道，但还是建吧”的功能，人们却很喜欢。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interesting.
turns.zh: 真有意思。

turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: Maybe I should just create an anti-me to do AI road-mapping.
turns.zh: 或许我应该创建一个反向的我来做人工智能路线图。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's in a simple agent right there, whatever Rahul says, do the opposite.
turns.zh: 这就需要一个简单的代理，只要拉胡尔说什么，就反着做。

turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. Another maybe a last topic. I know that you guys are starting to move into the enterprise. When people think of Superhuman, they think of it's consumer-y, it's for people, and you guys are doing a lot of work to make it a B2B enterprise product. For founders maybe that are starting to think about this transitioning from PLG to sales led and B2B enterprising, what have you learned about just what it takes to get to that point and what does that sales motion look like for you guys?
turns.zh: 好的。最后一个话题。我知道你们开始进军企业市场。当人们想到Superhuman时，他们会认为它面向消费者，适合个人使用，而你们正在努力将其打造成B2B企业产品。对于那些开始考虑从PLG模式转向销售驱动和B2B企业的创始人来说，你们从PLG到销售驱动和B2B转型的过程中，学到了哪些经验教训？销售策略是怎样的？

turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: In some ways, it's very like selling to prosumers, except these users are not coming from Gmail where prosumers would normally come from, they're coming from Outlook. And Outlook users have very different expectations to Gmail users. For example, Outlook users expect their email app to also be a fully featured calendar app, whereas Gmail users are happy with those two things being entirely different. As a result, we've invested in calendar very heavily and we continue to do so. There's only so much I can say, but it's pretty exciting.
turns.zh: 在某些方面，这很像向半专业用户销售产品，但这些用户不是来自Gmail（半专业用户通常来自Gmail），而是来自Outlook。Outlook用户对邮箱应用的期望与Gmail用户截然不同。例如，Outlook用户希望他们的邮箱应用同时也是一个功能齐全的日历应用，而Gmail用户则乐于接受这两者分开。因此，我们在日历功能上投入了大量精力，并将继续推进。虽然我不能透露太多细节，但这确实很令人兴奋。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: [inaudible 01:16:49].

turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: Outlook users are also used to certain safeguards, like if you've used Outlook in an enterprise, warnings when a recipient is external to your domain or what Outlook users might know as sensitivity labels. And as a result we've built support for external recipient indicators and sensitivity labels. But in some ways it's very different to selling to prosumers because there are other stakeholders involved. For example, we've built support for enterprise mobile management by implementing Microsoft Intune. (01:17:22): We recently sold one of the big three strategy consulting firms, which is super exciting. I can't say which one, but they love Superhuman and they have thousands of people internally using Superhuman. This is after a year... They've been piloting for a year and then accelerating over the last few months. We only just got them the mobile app, believe it or not. turns.speaker: Rahul Vohra
turns.en: SDR is a thinking tool that I picked up from Reid Hoffman during my time at LinkedIn. The idea here is that for important decisions, you should be able to identify one, one reason that on its own supports the decision. It's based on the observation that all too often we rely on a collection of weak reasons to justify decisions. It's very, very easy to do this. Imagine you are contemplating a decision, you write a list of the pros and the cons. There are three pros, but let's say there are 10 or 15 cons. The sheer number of cons, the effort of thinking them through, the time it took to write them down, is going to affect you, consciously or worse subconsciously. This is especially true, I've seen in group settings, which just in general are a little bit more risk averse and a little bit more consensus driven. (01:20:17): So whenever anyone is making a decision and they bring that decision to me and they say, "Well, we want to do this because of X, Y, Z, and there are multiple reasons." I ask them, "What's the SDR? What's the single decisive reason?" If they can't yet isolate it, that tells me they haven't yet figured out why they want to make the decision. It doesn't mean the decision is wrong, it just means that they haven't figured out the singular reason why we should do the thing. They can then go through their list of reasons and ask, "Is this alone enough to support this decision?" Meaning if this was true and all the other things were not true, would I still do it? And sometimes we still do, but actually sometimes we don't. We realize that a collection of weak reasons alone means that, for example, the outcome is less likely than we thought it was, or it was hiding a really strong reason on the other side of the decision.
turns.zh:
SDR是我在LinkedIn工作期间从里德·霍夫曼那里学到的一种思维工具。其核心理念是，对于重大决策，你应该能找出一个单一的、足以支撑该决策的核心理由。这源于一个观察：我们常常依赖一堆薄弱的理由来为决策辩护。这种做法其实非常容易理解。想象你正在考虑某个决定，列出利弊清单。可能有三个优点，但十个或十五个缺点。缺点数量之多、思考它们所耗费的精力，以及记录它们所花费的时间，都会潜意识或显意识地影响你的判断。尤其是在团队环境中，这种现象更为常见，因为团队通常更倾向于规避风险，更加追求共识。

（01:20:17）所以每当有人来找我做决策时，他们会说：“嗯，我们想这么做是因为X、Y、Z，还有多个理由。”我会问：“SDR是什么？单一决定性理由是什么？” 如果他们还无法明确，这说明他们还没有想清楚为什么要做这个决定。这并不意味着决策错误，只是说明他们没有找到支撑该决策的核心原因。接下来他们可以逐一检查每个理由，问：“仅凭这个理由足以支持这个决定吗？” 比如，如果这个理由是真的，而其他理由都是假的，你还会做吗？有时我们会坚持，有时则不会。我们会意识到，多个薄弱理由意味着结果的可能性比我们想象的要低，或者隐藏着一个决定另一侧的强大理由。

If we're going to build this for a collection of weak reasons, whereas we could build that for one strong reason, I'd much rather build that for one strong reason.
